claim: ToolJet AI is an AI-assisted app-building surface alongside ToolJet's visual app builder and connected data sources.

claim: ToolJet access control includes app promotion and release permissions and granular resource permissions.
falsifier: A current first-party access-control page denying promotion/release or granular resource permissions.

claim: ToolJet documents self-hosted AI gateway deployment with customer LLM keys and the ability to disable AI schema-reading data flow.
falsifier: A current first-party privacy page denying the on-premise gateway or administrator control over AI schema-reading.

claim: NocoBase AI Builder accepts natural-language business requirements and covers data modeling, UI, workflows, permissions and going live.
falsifier: A current first-party NocoBase AI Builder page limiting the feature to non-conversational design assistance.

claim: NocoBase distinguishes database-stored no-code portal configuration from AI Portal React source that can be committed to Git.
falsifier: A current first-party page stating both portal types produce only opaque hosted output.

claim: NocoBase AI-agent CLI operations can be recorded in audit logs with executor, resource, result and CLI request-source metadata.
falsifier: A current first-party security page denying audit records for CLI-initiated critical operations.

claim: Appsmith documents internal apps built from widgets, queries, APIs and JavaScript.
falsifier: A current first-party Appsmith docs page stating those are not app-building primitives.

claim: Appsmith documentation retains open-source deployment choices for internal applications.
falsifier: A current first-party Appsmith page stating deployment is exclusively vendor-hosted.

falsifier: A current first-party Builder page stating the surface produces no frontend code or UI output.

claim: Builder.io positions component integration and CMS context as part of the design-to-code workflow.
falsifier: A current first-party Builder page denying component-oriented integration or CMS context.

claim: Visily Export to Code supports React, Vue and HTML and packages the result as a downloadable ZIP.
falsifier: A current Visily support page removing all three code formats or ZIP download.

claim: Visily's AI layout export consumes AI credits while static layout does not, and code export is limited to supported paid plans.
falsifier: A current Visily export page denying the paid-plan gate or the AI-credit distinction.

claim: Uizard pricing lists Autodesigner and text generation for projects, screens, themes, images and design reviews.
falsifier: A current Uizard pricing page removing Autodesigner or all text-generation capabilities.

claim: Uizard offers developer handoff in React and CSS on paid plans.
falsifier: A current Uizard pricing page denying React/CSS developer handoff.

claim: Uizard exposes plan-gated AI generation quotas, including 3, 500, 5,000 or unlimited generations in the observed plan table.

claim: Locofy can import a Figma URL, convert it to frontend code, refine it in Builder and export it.
falsifier: A current Locofy quickstart denying URL import or frontend-code conversion.

claim: Locofy supports code download, CLI, MCP, GitHub sync and VS Code export/integration paths.
falsifier: A current Locofy page denying these export/integration paths.

claim: Locofy documents that generated code can be pushed to GitHub but Builder does not sync GitHub code back into Builder.
falsifier: A current Locofy troubleshooting page documenting bidirectional code sync or denying GitHub push.

claim: Modal Sandboxes are secure containers for untrusted or model-generated code with configurable CPU, memory and lifetime.
falsifier: A current Modal sandbox guide denying isolation or configurable resource/lifetime controls.

claim: Modal supports filesystem, directory and memory snapshots that can restore sandbox state, with documented TTL and process limitations.
falsifier: A current Modal snapshot guide denying restore or changing the documented snapshot limitations.

claim: Modal Sandboxes have no inbound network by default and support full outbound blocking or CIDR/domain allowlists.
falsifier: A current Modal networking page denying default inbound blocking or outbound controls.

claim: Daytona sandboxes provide isolated kernel, filesystem, network stack and allocated vCPU/RAM/disk, with container, VM and GPU classes.
falsifier: A current Daytona sandbox page denying per-sandbox isolation or those runtime classes.

claim: Daytona documents stop/start persistence, filesystem and memory snapshots, VM pause/resume, forks and volumes as persistence mechanisms.
falsifier: A current Daytona persistence page denying those mechanisms or their stated class limitations.

claim: Daytona bills reserved sandbox resources using pay-as-you-go pricing, with per-second vCPU, RAM and disk accounting.
falsifier: A current Daytona billing page denying resource-based pay-as-you-go accounting.

claim: E2B presents a cloud sandbox/runtime surface for AI agents and code actions.
falsifier: A current E2B product page stating E2B does not provide sandbox/runtime infrastructure for agents or code.

claim: E2B pricing separates subscription tiers from usage costs and publishes session-length, concurrency and per-second resource pricing controls.
falsifier: A current E2B pricing page denying separate usage costs or the documented session/concurrency/resource model.
